title: 5 Reasons why Bro Splits are Garbage
summary: NH gives five reasons natural lifters should avoid bro splits (one body part per day, each trained once a week). Big and small muscles get the same frequency, leg day becomes dreaded, days get wasted on things like abs, lagging muscles such as calves develop, and the format pushes isolation over compounds. He dismisses the volume-equated frequency study used to revive bro splits and recommends push/pull/legs, upper/lower, full body or gentleman splits.
claims: A bro split means one body part per day (a triceps day, an abs day); grouping chest, shoulders and triceps together is a gentleman split, not a bro split
Treating the body as separate puzzle pieces makes no sense because muscles work together, and training should use that
Frequency is as important as volume and intensity in the holy trinity of programming; remove one and you damage the other two

The recent study showing equal hypertrophy at once versus three times a week with volume equated is flawed, because higher frequency lets you accumulate more volume, so volume is never equal in practice
Even with equal volume, splitting it over three days still gives better gains because of returning to baseline, recovery and intensity windows
Bro splits give triceps and legs the same weekly frequency even though muscle size affects recovery and how much volume and frequency a muscle needs
Triceps fatigue fast in one weekly session and could be trained again three days later; legs could be crushed and trained again four days later
Bro splits breed hatred of leg day because all leg tonnage is crammed into one brutal session, which is why bro splitters often have small legs
Training a muscle only once a week leaves it unconditioned, so recovery is poor and soreness is severe
A dedicated abs day is a wasted day; superset abs through the week for more volume, and use that day for a second leg day
You will not grow big calves training them once a week, whatever the volume or intensity, unless you were previously fat or have great genetics; they need several recovery windows a week
Bro splits push too much isolation; an upper-body day with no horizontal or vertical press is pointless
Compounds must make up the vast majority of a natural's training; a program that is 75% isolation is garbage, and that is how enhanced pro bodybuilders train
Bro split promoters are either contrarians seeking attention or people who ignore progression and train by the pump
Growth comes from strength progression over time leading to more tonnage, not from the pump; ask a bro splitter how much his squat went up this year and he will not know
Natural lifters on bro splits stay small, and big bro splitters are not natural
Use push/pull/legs, upper/lower, full body or gentleman splits as the main hypertrophy templates
